html:
Bernardo O'Higgins was a Chilean independence leader and the first head of state of independent Chile, as Supreme Director from 1817 to 1823. He is called the father of the nation.

The illegitimate son of an Irish-born viceroy of Peru, he was educated in England, where he met the revolutionary Francisco de Miranda. He led patriot troops after 1810, was beaten in 1814, and fled across the Andes. With José de San Martín he crossed back in 1817 and won at Chacabuco, then at Maipú in 1818.

He declared independence in 1818 and ruled as a reforming dictator, abolishing titles of nobility and founding schools. His high-handed rule turned the landowners and the Church against him, and he was forced to resign in 1823. He died in exile in Peru. He is the founding hero of Chile.
